features.description: Release manifest contract with UX-critical fields (pure schema + model + loader module; no CLI). Define upgrade-releases.schema.json (+ Pydantic model in claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models, with an agent-conventions VERSION bump) and load_release_manifest. The manifest is an object with a top-level baseline (D018: baseline_release id + baseline_date — CHANGELOG sections at/before this baseline are intentionally NOT manifest-seeded; the F009 coverage lint only flags operator-visible sections AFTER the baseline that lack an entry, so the 'covers the changelog' promise is scoped and cannot silently drift) and an ordered releases[] list. Each release has: stable id, date (YYYY-MM-DD string), plan_refs[], summary, show_on_first_run (bool, default false — see F004 first-run policy), and actions[]. Each action carries enough to tell the user WHY, WHETHER IT APPLIES, and WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (D004, D013): id, kind (closed enum required|advisory), severity (optional closed enum critical|recommended|optional), title, detail (the why), commands[] (D017: ORDERED list for safe migrations — each {label closed enum preview|apply|verify|run, command string, description optional}; empty/omitted for advisories — replaces a single command field so preview->apply->verify is first-class), introduced_commands (optional array of new CLI surfaces the release adds), applies_when (optional predicate key; null=always applies), status_probe (optional predicate key; null=advisory/no probe — sole authority for required-action satisfaction, D004), success_message (optional), failure_message (optional), human_next_step (optional), docs_url (optional), evidence_uri (optional). The manifest (NOT prose CHANGELOG, NOT the plan ledger; D002) is the single machine source of truth for upgrade intent. Schema is closed: unknown kind/severity/label values and unknown keys are rejected fail-closed. REQUIRED-ACTION INVARIANT (D021): a kind=required action MUST name a non-null, non-empty status_probe; the loader rejects a required action with null/empty status_probe (such an action could never be cleared by a live probe). kind=advisory actions may omit status_probe. REQUIRED-COMMAND INVARIANT (D029): a kind=required action MUST have a non-empty commands[] that includes at least an apply-labeled command (the state-changing operator step); the loader rejects a required action with empty commands or with no apply-labeled command, so a required action always yields an exact copyable command. Advisory actions may have empty commands. ID-UNIQUENESS INVARIANT (D030): the loader rejects duplicate release ids across the manifest and duplicate action ids within a single release, so the stable id upgrade:<release>:<action> can never collide and releases_since is unambiguous. ORDERED-CHECKLIST INVARIANT (D036, refines D029): a kind=required action's commands[] MUST include at least an apply-labeled AND a verify-labeled command, in label order (preview optional, must precede apply); the loader rejects a required action missing apply or verify, or with out-of-order labels, so a required action always presents the ordered preview->apply->verify checklist the operator follows. MANIFEST RESOLUTION (D045): load_release_manifest resolves docs/upgrade/releases.json as a PACKAGE-RELATIVE resource (shipped with the dontpanic distribution), so it loads when the CLI is invoked outside the repo root, from an installed package, and off-git; resolution does not depend on the current working directory or git metadata. The required-command invariant also rejects a blank/whitespace-only command string (D047): every command in a required action's commands[] must be a non-blank exact string, upholding the exact-copyable-command promise.

features.description: Detection predicate registry (status_probes + applies_when) as a pure core module. A predicate maps a key to a callable returning {satisfied, detail, evidence_uri}. status_probe is the ONLY authority for whether a REQUIRED action is satisfied (the marker never satisfies a required action, D004). applies_when keys gate whether an action is shown to THIS instance at all. canonical_discovery_registered_active (status_probe) is an OUTCOME probe — satisfied iff DontPanic resolves to registered_active via the canonical-discovery reconcile path. EVIDENCE-COUPLING RULE (D019): evidence validity does NOT gate an already-proven outcome; if registered_active is true the action is satisfied even with a stale/malformed leftover backfill-evidence file. Evidence validity blocks ONLY a separate evidence-consuming predicate canonical_backfill_evidence_valid, used where remaining work depends on that evidence and the outcome is not yet proven. has_tracked_projects (applies_when) is satisfied iff a non-empty project registry exists. Predicates degrade honestly: status_probe undeterminable -> not satisfied (fail-closed); applies_when undeterminable -> applies true (never silently hide a required action). UNKNOWN-KEY FAIL-CLOSED (D026): resolving an unknown status_probe key yields a fail-closed result (satisfied=false with an explicit error detail) so a typo can never satisfy or silently hide a required action; an unknown applies_when key yields applies=true with an error detail (surface it, never silently drop). Neither crashes report assembly. NO-MUTATION CONTRACT (D028): every predicate is a strictly READ-ONLY observation; it MUST NOT write or modify registry, evidence, config, ledger, or any on-disk state. canonical_discovery_registered_active reuses ONLY the read/reconcile path of canonical-discovery, never a write path. This upholds the user-facing no-mutation invariant during any read-only command.

Assert no-mutation: a test runs every predicate against a fixture HOME/registry and asserts zero writes (no registry/evidence/config/ledger/state mutation)

Tests cover every state. An unknown status_probe key resolves to satisfied=false with an error detail (never satisfied), and an unknown applies_when key to applies=true with an error detail; neither crashes assembly (dedicated tests). Every predicate is read-only: a dedicated test runs each predicate and asserts NO registry/evidence/config/ledger/state mutation occurs (no-mutation contract, D028); canonical_discovery_registered_active uses only the reconcile read path. Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

features.description: Per-instance upgrade-state marker + releases-since diff + FIRST-RUN policy as a core/persistence module with a NO-SILENT-WRITE consent invariant (D015). The on-disk marker upgrade-state.json (HOME-resolved under ~/.dontpanic) holds last_seen_release, last_seen_commit, dismissed_advisories[], first_initialized_at. CONSENT INVARIANT: write_upgrade_state is invoked ONLY by the acknowledge/dismiss path (F007); read_upgrade_state, when the file is absent, returns an IN-MEMORY effective marker (anchored to the latest release) WITHOUT persisting it, so a read can never silently suppress advisories. releases_since(marker, manifest) purely computes releases newer than last_seen_release in manifest order. FIRST-RUN POLICY (D012): a fresh in-memory marker shows only first_run_advisories (releases flagged show_on_first_run) — the full advisory history is not replayed — while required actions stay probe-driven regardless of marker. advance_marker and dismiss_advisory are pure transforms over the marker value; persistence happens only on the F007 acknowledge path. MARKER-PREDATES / UNKNOWN-RELEASE (D035, reconciled by D040/D044): when last_seen_release is absent from the manifest OR orders before the earliest manifest release, releases_since treats the marker as positioned before all manifest releases (every manifest release is new); ADVISORY filtering is then governed by marker_state per the three-case rule (an EXISTING predating marker shows ALL advisories; only a truly ABSENT marker applies the show_on_first_run filter). releases_since never raises on an unknown/stale last_seen_release. THREE MARKER CASES (D040/D042), with an explicit marker_state field (absent|predates|known): (a) ABSENT marker (no file ever = fresh install): the in-memory effective marker anchors to the LATEST release so history is NOT replayed; only show_on_first_run advisories are shown; marker_state=absent and the displayed acknowledgement (last_seen_release/last_seen_commit) is NULL / 'never acknowledged' (never implies the operator acknowledged latest). (b) EXISTING marker whose last_seen_release predates the earliest manifest release OR is absent-from-manifest (a real UPGRADE from an old version): treat as before-all so ALL manifest releases are new and ALL their advisories are shown (the show_on_first_run filter does NOT apply here - this is an upgrade, not a fresh install); marker_state=predates. (c) EXISTING in-manifest marker: releases_since(last_seen) newer releases with their advisories; marker_state=known. releases_since/first_run_advisories never raise; marker_state is returned alongside the effective marker.

features.description: Upgrade-readiness report assembly with the version/update summary + UPSTREAM availability, as a pure core function (no CLI). assemble_upgrade_report(manifest, marker, predicate_registry) combines releases_since/first-run (F004), evaluates applies_when + status_probe (F003), and returns {summary, required[], advisory[], migration_status[]}. The summary (D010) carries installed_commit (git HEAD short, 'unknown' off-git), latest_release_id (last manifest release), last_seen_release (from marker), pending_required (count), pending_advisory (count), update_state (closed enum up_to_date | required_pending | advisories_pending | unknown), and an UPSTREAM block (D016): fetched_upstream_commit (the tracked upstream ref's commit AS ALREADY KNOWN LOCALLY — read-only, NO network fetch by default) and upstream_status (closed enum up_to_date | behind | ahead | diverged | unknown) plus a remediation hint. upstream_status answers 'am I behind the newest DontPanic?', is 'unknown' off-git/no-upstream/never-fetched, and is computed WITHOUT an implicit network fetch (an opt-in flag in F006 may refresh). A required action is 'pending' iff its status_probe is not satisfied AND applies_when holds — independent of the marker. required[] items carry the action's ordered commands + success/failure copy + human_next_step + docs_url; advisory[] respects first-run + dismissals; migration_status[] is probe-backed. SUMMARY also carries last_seen_commit from the marker (D023) — distinct from installed_commit (current checkout) — so the dashboard can show the ACKNOWLEDGED commit. Each required[] item also carries the action's introduced_commands (D022) so the report can tell operators which new command surfaces landed. migration_status[] items have a PINNED contract (D024): release id, action id, applies status, probe key, satisfied flag, a human detail, and an evidence pointer. Report assembly surfaces unknown-predicate-key error details from F003 rather than crashing (D026). introduced_commands is attached to BOTH required[] and advisory[] report items (D033), so advisory-only releases still tell operators what newly exists. PINNED ITEM SHAPE (D041): every required[] and advisory[] report item carries a stable item id (upgrade:<release>:<action>), release id, action id, kind, severity, title, detail, applies (bool from applies_when), the ordered commands (each label+command), success_message, failure_message, human_next_step, docs_url, introduced_commands, and - when the action has a status_probe - satisfied plus a probe detail. The same shape is used for required[] and advisory[] so renderers and ActionItems read one contract. The summary reflects marker_state from F004: when marker_state=absent, last_seen_release and last_seen_commit render as 'never acknowledged' (null), never as the latest release/commit (D042). Each report item also carries the ORIGINAL applies_when and status_probe keys (D046) alongside the resolved applies/satisfied values, so manifest-sourced upgrade intent stays auditable in the JSON output. migration_status[] INCLUSION RULE (D051): it lists EVERY probe-backed action with its current state (pending, satisfied, or not-applicable), not only pending ones, so a satisfied or not-applicable canonical-discovery item still appears and the migration audit/JSON stays complete across runs.

features.description: `dontpanic doctor` CLI integration (read-only render). Wire assemble_upgrade_report (F005) into doctor: plain `dontpanic doctor` adds exactly one concise WARN CheckResult summarizing pending_required/pending_advisory (and an upstream-behind note when known) with the remediation command when anything pends; the --upgrade flag prints the full human report led by the version/update + upstream summary; the --upgrade --json flag emits the machine-readable report (summary + upstream + required[]/advisory[]/migration_status[]); an optional --check-upstream flag opts into a network fetch before computing upstream_status. All these render paths are READ-ONLY w.r.t. the marker (they never call write_upgrade_state; F004 D015). The report also surfaces each required action's introduced_commands (D022) — the new command surfaces the release added — in both the human report and the JSON output, so operators see what newly exists. introduced_commands is rendered for advisory items as well as required (D033), in both human and JSON, so advisory releases that add commands are visible. END-TO-END NO-MUTATION (D050): a test runs the full plain doctor and the upgrade report path against a fixture instance and asserts ZERO writes anywhere - no backfill, migration, config, registry, evidence, ledger, or marker write - not only the probe (F003) and marker (D015) sub-checks. The acknowledge path (F007) is the sole writer.

features.description: Acknowledge path — the ONLY marker-write surface (D015). Add the --acknowledge flag to `dontpanic doctor`: it calls advance_marker (F004) to the latest release and dismiss_advisory for currently-shown advisories, commits the result via F004's write_upgrade_state, then re-renders. CRITICAL INVARIANT (D004): the acknowledge flag advances the marker and silences advisory noise ONLY; it does NOT clear a required action whose status_probe still fails — such an action remains pending after acknowledge. LEGAL COMBINATIONS (D027): the acknowledge flag composes with the upgrade report mode in both human and JSON form; after acknowledging, the re-rendered report (human or JSON) reflects the ADVANCED marker (advisories silenced, last_seen_release/last_seen_commit updated) while any probe-failing required action still shows pending. Acknowledge without the upgrade report mode still advances the marker and prints a concise confirmation.

Acknowledge composes with the upgrade report mode in human and JSON form; the post-acknowledge report reflects the advanced marker (advisories silenced, last_seen_release/last_seen_commit updated) while a probe-failing required action still shows pending (dedicated tests, D027). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

features.description: Dashboard update-status visibility (standing signal) + ActionItem drill-down. From the F005 summary, project an always-rendered upgrade-readiness STATUS signal (upgrade_status_projection) shown as a Tools & Setup / Health row: a single line from update_state + counts + last_seen_release + installed_commit — e.g. 'DontPanic: up to date' / 'DontPanic: 2 upgrade actions pending' / 'Last acknowledged: 2026-06-17 (commit abc1234)'. This row is ALWAYS shown, including the positive up-to-date case (D011). ActionItems remain the DRILL-DOWN (upgrade_action_items): a probe-pending required action -> band=needs_action with its first apply-labeled command; an undismissed advisory -> band=advisory; satisfied/dismissed absent or info. source='upgrade'; ids are stable (upgrade:<release>:<action>) and sorted by a stable key. Both projections go through the existing dashboard state/action_view shape and carry no secret shapes. The status projection ALSO carries upstream_status (D031): the row reflects 'behind the newest DontPanic' when the known upstream is behind, so it never renders 'up to date' while upstream_status is behind. update_state (manifest-action readiness) and upstream_status (code-level freshness) are distinct and both shown. The projection carries last_seen_commit (from the marker) AND installed_commit separately: the LAST-ACKNOWLEDGED display uses last_seen_commit while installed_commit is shown as the current checkout; the two are never conflated (D037). When marker_state=absent the status row shows 'never acknowledged' rather than a last-acknowledged release/commit, so a fresh install is never misreported as having acknowledged the latest release (D042). features.description: End-to-end 'after git pull' update journey through the real doctor CLI, captured as evidence (D014; operator-outcome QA). update_journey_e2e drives the real `dontpanic doctor` surface: from an instance whose marker predates the seeded releases (or has none) on a known commit, plain doctor surfaces the WARN with pending counts; the upgrade report (JSON) shows the summary + the canonical-discovery required action pending; after the status_probe is made to return satisfied, a re-run clears the required action and plain doctor no longer WARNs for it, with update_state transitioning. The captured upgrade report (real probe on the live instance) and the journey transcript are saved under evidence/. Marker write/no-write assertions live in F004/F007; this feature asserts the CLI journey + update_state transition only. The journey satisfies the required action by running its REAL copyable command path (the verify-labeled command from the manifest), not a direct fixture toggle (D025), so a broken preview/apply/verify command is caught by the e2e rather than masked. CORRECTION (D032, supersedes the D025 narrowing): the journey satisfies the required action by running its APPLY-labeled command (the real state-changing migration step), then the verify-labeled command PROVES the resulting state; satisfaction is never driven by the verify command alone (verify proves, it does not create) nor by a fixture toggle. A broken apply OR verify command fails the journey. SINGLE SATISFYING PATH (D038): the ONLY way the journey clears the required action is run-apply-then-verify; there is no verify-alone or fixture-toggle satisfying path anywhere in this feature. MUTATION ISOLATION (D043): the apply-labeled (state-changing) command runs ONLY against a DISPOSABLE, ISOLATED fixture instance (a temp DONTPANIC_HOME + fixture registry), NEVER the operator's real DontPanic registry; the isolated instance is torn down after the journey. The live read of the real instance is limited to the read-only upgrade report capture (no apply against the real registry).
